recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的大細胞內沒有核膜，兩團濃縮、呈絲狀的染色體分別位於細胞兩極，中間隔著淡色區域，細胞質仍連成一體尚未分裂，符合有絲分裂後期（anaphase）。
features: Large cell with two separate clusters of condensed, spiky chromosomes at opposite poles
No nuclear membrane; clear cytoplasmic zone between the two chromosome sets
Single continuous cytoplasm without a cleavage furrow
Pale gray-blue cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules, suggesting a granulocytic precursor
Cellular background with myeloid precursors, erythroblasts, and disrupted smudged cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is cellular with a mixture of granulocytic and erythroid precursors and occasional disrupted cells. The arrowed cell contains two separate aggregates of condensed chromosomes at opposite poles within a single, undivided cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules, without a nuclear membrane or cleavage furrow. This is a mitotic figure in anaphase, most likely in a granulocytic precursor. No multipolar figure or lagging chromosomes are seen. Findings are consistent with a normal anaphase mitotic figure.

ddx.vs: A binucleate cell has two intact nuclei with nuclear membranes and a regular chromatin pattern rather than naked condensed chromosome clusters.
Telophase shows a cleavage furrow and reforming rounded daughter nuclei, which are absent here.
A multipolar mitosis shows three or more chromosome groups or lagging chromosomes rather than two symmetric poles.
Apoptotic nuclear fragments are smooth, round, and homogeneously dense instead of filamentous chromosome arms.
